attribution.note: Marcus's own words in a published conversation transcript on his Substack.

semantics.note: 'I think OpenAI is gonna' is an unqualified expectation, not on the hedge list, so it counts as a forecast. 'At some point' is kept as an open horizon. The proposition drops 'really', a minor softener.

contract.note: The plain reading (default, missed payments, forced restructuring, or insolvency) is the ordinary meaning of 'can't meet their obligations'. Saying the claim can't be contradicted without a deadline is fair.

evidence.note: Q1 2026 figures, published June 20: more than $73B in cash and securities. Shows no current inability to pay. Doesn't settle an open-ended forecast.
April 2026 report of missed sales and user targets, and partner worries. No default or missed payment reported.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-horizon forecast that OpenAI will be unable to meet its obligations. The packet shows no default, missed payment, or insolvency by the cutoff, so the early-resolution rule isn't met. With no deadline, the absence of a default isn't a failure. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own prose in Part II of his post.

semantics.note: A structural economic claim: a reliable product forces a choice between high prices and losses. The 'reliable version' qualifier and 'want to pay' are kept.

contract.note: 'Reliable version of the product' is undefined and 'more than customers want to pay' has no threshold, so no observable test exists. Treating the claim as not adjudicable is fair.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 shows an 85% implied gross margin in H1 2026 on current products. That isn't the undefined 'reliable version'.
Heavy agent use on flat plans was underpriced, which fits his framing. It doesn't test the reliable-product cost claim.

reviews.rationale: The claim depends on the cost and willingness to pay for a 'reliable version' of LLM products, which Marcus doesn't define and which can't be measured. Current margins and pricing changes are context only. Not adjudicable.

attribution.note: Marcus speaking in his own voice in the transcribed conversation.

semantics.note: A present-tense observation about shifting business market position. The normalised wording matches it.

contract.note: Reading 'business market' as enterprise share from about 2023 is an ordinary, fair reading. It is neither stretched nor restricted to customer losses.

evidence.note: Menlo's survey: Anthropic's enterprise LLM API share rose from 12% to 40% and OpenAI's fell from 50% to 27% (2023 to 2025). Menlo is an Anthropic investor, but the measurement is still credible.
Ramp: Anthropic overtook OpenAI in business adoption in April 2026, while OpenAI's adoption was roughly flat over the year. Different denominator; it is consistent with relative share loss.

reviews.rationale: Under the share-based plain reading, Menlo shows a large gain for Anthropic and a large loss for OpenAI in enterprise LLM API share. Ramp independently shows Anthropic overtaking OpenAI in business adoption by April 2026. Ramp's flat OpenAI adoption limits a customer-loss reading but not the share claim. Supported.

attribution.note: Marcus's own prose in Part III of his post.

semantics.note: The antecedent (market-forced IPO withdrawal or a sharp cut in aspirations) and the 'I don't see how' wording are kept. The $600B figure is kept as stated.

contract.note: Requiring a market-forced withdrawal or sharp cut, rather than a mere postponement, follows his words. The basis of the $600B figure is unspecified, which the contract flags.

evidence.note: Altman ruled out a 2026 IPO and cited safety. That is a postponement, not a market-forced withdrawal. The antecedent is not established.
Secondary summary: listing likely in H1 2027 and the private valuation target trimmed. It doesn't show IPO withdrawal or sharply cut IPO terms.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast. The evidence shows only a postponement for stated safety reasons, not a market-forced withdrawal or sharp cut, so the antecedent isn't established. No default or fulfillment is shown, and there is no deadline. Not scored: unresolved.
